proof_route.method: Explicit finite tensor kernel; no analytic or Boolean-analysis axioms
steps: Factor patternWeight into per-coordinate Bernoulli weights.
Apply mathlib Finset.prod_one_add to factor the character kernel sum.
Check the four membership cases of the weighted one-coordinate kernel, using sqrt(p*(1-p))^2=p*(1-p).
Multiply coordinate delta kernels to obtain the weighted full delta kernel.
Represent the character kernel by a finite square matrix M and weighted transpose N; M*N=1 implies N*M=1, proving character orthogonality.
Interchange finite sums to obtain Fourier inversion.
Interchange finite sums again to obtain bilinear Parseval.
The empty Fourier coefficient is the expectation, so subtracting its square gives precisely the frozen variance statement.
proof_route.strictly_useful: The scalar coordinate calculation and tensor kernel are elementary independent identities. Inversion and bilinear Parseval supply reusable identities for energy and noise. No step assumes the Parseval target or a sharp-threshold ancestor.
